- Videos: Extract thumbnail at 1s, store duration/dimensions

- Videos extract thumbnail automatically
- Media library shows all uploads with filtering
- Can select media to add to portfolio sections

- Phase 1 database schema (media table exists)

title: Implement ZIP packaging service
description:
Create service to package all export components into a downloadable ZIP file.

- Stream ZIP creation for memory efficiency
- Support large media files without loading all into memory
- Set proper file permissions in ZIP

## Implementation
- Create `lib/export/packager.ts`

- Function: `createExportPackage(data: ExportPackage): ReadableStream`

## Package Structure
```
portfolio-export.zip
├── index.html              # Main site
├── manifest.json           # Portfolio metadata
├── README.md              # Deployment instructions
├── assets/
│   ├── styles.css         # If separated
│   └── fonts/
│       ├── fonts.css
│       └── *.woff2
└── media/
    ├── images/
    │   └── *.jpg, *.png, *.webp
    └── videos/
        └── *.mp4, *.webm
```

## Dependencies
- `archiver` or `jszip` npm package

## Streaming
```typescript
const archive = archiver('zip', { zlib: { level: 6 } })
archive.append(htmlContent, { name: 'index.html' })
archive.directory('media/', 'media')
return archive
```

title: Add export analytics and rate limiting
description:
Track export usage and prevent abuse.

## Analytics
Track in database or analytics service:
- Export initiated (portfolioId, userId, timestamp)
- Export completed (success/failure, file size, duration)
- Export options used (videos included, fonts embedded)

## Rate Limiting
- Limit exports per user: 10 per day
- Limit export file size: 500MB max
- Return 429 if rate limit exceeded with retry-after header

## Implementation
```typescript
// Check rate limit before export
const recentExports = await db
  .select()
  .from(exportLogs)
  .where(and(
    eq(exportLogs.userId, userId),
    gt(exportLogs.createdAt, dayAgo)
  ))

if (recentExports.length >= 10) {
  return new Response('Rate limit exceeded', { status: 429 })
}
```

## Database Schema Addition
```sql
CREATE TABLE export_logs (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id uuid REFERENCES users(id),
  portfolio_id uuid REFERENCES portfolios(id),
  file_size bigint,
  include_videos boolean,
  embed_fonts boolean,
  status text, -- 'started', 'completed', 'failed'
  error_message text,
  created_at timestamp DEFAULT now(),
  completed_at timestamp
);
```

title: Implement font embedding for offline use
description:
Handle Google Fonts to ensure exported sites work offline.

## Problem
AI-generated HTML portfolios use Google Fonts (Space Grotesk, Instrument Serif, etc.) loaded from CDN. For true self-hosting, fonts should be embedded.

## Options
1. **Embed fonts** - Download font files, include in export
2. **Keep CDN links** - Simpler, requires internet connection
3. **User choice** - Let user decide via export options

## Implementation
- Create `lib/export/font-handler.ts`
- Parse HTML for Google Fonts links
- Download font files (.woff2) from Google Fonts CSS
- Generate local `assets/fonts.css` with @font-face rules
- Rewrite HTML to use local font CSS

## Font Extraction
1. Find: `<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=...">`
2. Fetch CSS, parse @font-face rules
3. Download each .woff2 file
4. Generate local CSS pointing to downloaded files
5. Replace Google Fonts link with local CSS

## Output
```
assets/
└── fonts/
    ├── fonts.css
    ├── space-grotesk-400.woff2
    ├── space-grotesk-700.woff2
    └── instrument-serif-400.woff2
```

// components/dashboard/export-button.tsx
export function ExportButton({ portfolioId }: { portfolioId: string }) {
  const [isExporting, setIsExporting] = useState(false)

      body: JSON.stringify(options)
    })

    downloadBlob(blob, 'portfolio-export.zip')

}

   - Increment portfolioViewCount on user record

4. If recent view exists:
   - Skip incrementing (return success but don't count)

## Files to modify

- app/api/portfolio/track/route.ts - subdomain-based tracking endpoint

title: Implement static HTML generation for JSON portfolios
description:
Generate static HTML from JSON-based portfolios that don't have stored HTML content.

## Context
Portfolios have two types:
- `portfolioType: 'html'` - Already have complete HTML in `htmlContent`
- `portfolioType: 'json'` - Need to render to static HTML

## Implementation
- Create `lib/export/html-generator.ts`
- Function: `generateStaticHtml(data: ExportData): Promise<string>`
- Render portfolio sections to HTML matching the React components
- Inline all CSS styles
- Include responsive meta tags and proper DOCTYPE

## HTML Structure
```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>{portfolio.title}</title>
  <style>/* Inlined Tailwind-like CSS */</style>
  <link href="assets/fonts.css" rel="stylesheet">
</head>
<body>
  <!-- Rendered sections -->
</body>
</html>
```

## Section Types to Support
- hero: Full-width hero with headline, CTA
- about: Bio section with image
- work: Portfolio grid/gallery
- services: Service offerings
- contact: Contact info (form replaced with mailto link)
- testimonials: Client testimonials
- custom: Custom HTML sections

## Styling
- Extract critical CSS from Tailwind
- Support theme colors from portfolio.theme
- Ensure responsive design works without JS
